findings.title: Required E2E test bullet was rewritten after implementation to drop the real-CLI configured-reranker case; no test runs the CLI recall with a configured reranker and observes a populated scores.reranker
findings.evidence: Staged phase-doc diff (roadmap/phase-100640-rerank-relevance-normalization.md): the Required Tests bullet '- [ ] End-to-end tests (real CLI/MCP `recall` with a configured reranker shows `scores.reranker`)' was replaced by '- [x] End-to-end tests (MCP in-process `retrieve` ... ; CLI JSON shares the same binding and asserts the `scores` key contract)'. Repo scan: no test under crates/clio-lib configures a reranker (grep 'set_reranker|build_reranker_from|rerank_active' matches only clio-retrieve and clio-mcp); crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_scores_tests.rs:155 and :231 assert scores["reranker"] == null, i.e. only the no-reranker case. The only populated case runs through crates/clio-mcp/src/index_drain_tests.rs:211-218 (in-process MCP dispatch). Developer's own summary states: 'the MCP in-process pipeline (not the CLI binary itself) carried the configured-rerank end-to-end test, with the CLI JSON sharing the same binding'.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100640 §8 Required Tests (E2E bullet, original text); §9 AC-100640-04; task rule 'Never mark complete while such an item is silently skipped'
findings.recommendation: Add a CLI recall test with a configured fake reranker sidecar that asserts a populated numeric scores.reranker (clio-lib already has run_state plus fake HTTP server helpers), or restore the original bullet and record the CLI gap explicitly as an owner-approved limitation instead of rewriting the criterion.
findings.resolution: Implemented the recommendation's first branch. New test `recall_json_reranker_is_populated_with_configured_reranker` at crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_scores_tests.rs:394 (file now 447 lines, <=450) runs the real CLI `recall` verb (`run_state`) against `McpState::open_with_effective` with an effective `rerank` block (`{"url": <local double>, "model": "fake-rerank-tei", "provider": "tei"}`), so `build_reranker_from`/`set_reranker` attach the second stage exactly as the binary does. Supporting items in the same file: `FakeRerank` double with `read_request` (Content-Length-bounded), `rerank_body` (answers the received `texts` with the reversed permutation, `index = count-1-rank`, `score = 0.9-0.1*rank`), `fake_rerank_server` (non-blocking bounded accept loop, stop flag, 5s stream read timeout, joined with the served count) and `state_with_reranker`. Assertions: `state.pipeline.rerank_active`; exit 0 and empty stderr; `cli["reranked"] == true`; `served >= 1` after join; `hits.len() == texts.len() >= 2`; per hit `scores.reranker` a populated number equal to the exact `0.9-0.1*position` value (`< f64::EPSILON`) in [0,1], the hit's gist contained in `texts[len-1-position]` (provider order applied AND bound to the right document), `scores.final == score`, `scores.semantic` null, `scores.keyword` numeric. The double is stopped and joined, so no listener/thread leaks. The phase §8 Required Tests E2E bullet was rewritten back to the real-CLI wording now that the case exists. Non-vacuity: the worker ran two temporary negative controls (expected score start 0.85 instead of 0.9 -> FAILED with the real payload showing a populated 0.9 bound to the first output hit; flipped provider-index mapping -> FAILED the gist binding assertion), then reverted both and re-ran green. Real output: `cargo test -p clio --locked` -> 'test result: ok. 582 passed; 0 failed' plus all integration/doc targets ok (parent re-ran this independently); worker's focused run: 'test cli_read::tests::scores_tests::recall_json_reranker_is_populated_with_configured_reranker ... ok / test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed'. Clippy/fmt clean, 447 lines (<=450).
findings.evidence_after: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_scores_tests.rs:394-447; `cargo test -p clio --locked` 582 passed / 0 failed (round 1); full `make check` exit 0 with 2455 tests passed / 0 failed (round 2, delivered tree).

findings.title: Index-only response bodies that previously reordered now fail the whole rerank, changing the results[]/bare-array compatibility semantics listed under 'Must Not Change'
findings.evidence: Pre-change parser accepted index-only entries: deleted test parse_results_order_appends_omitted_documents ran on {"results":[{"index":2},{"index":0}]} and expected order [2,0,1] (staged diff of crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_tests.rs). New crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_parse.rs:192-198 (entry_score) errors when a present entry lacks a numeric score (call sites at :113-120 and :126-133), and rerank_tests.rs:88 asserts parse_rerank_response(&json!([{"index":0}]),2).is_err(). On such input the orchestrator now keeps the fused order and emits the 'rerank unavailable' warning instead of applying the provider order. Phase §2 'Must Not Change' says: 'The results[]/scores[]/bare-array compatibility semantics (now also reading scores)' must hold; §5 Task 2 says a missing score 'fails closed'; §10 says a missing score must 'Emit null'. Completion evidence records the fail-closed choice but does not disclose or resolve the compatibility change, and DoD 'Existing behavior remains intact' is checked [x].
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100640 §2 Must Not Change (compatibility semantics); §5 Task 2; §8 T100640-03; §10 Failure Handling
findings.recommendation: Owner decides: either keep fail-closed and record the deliberate compatibility break in Known Limitations/Completion Evidence, or preserve compatibility by carrying score: None for a present entry without a numeric score (order preserved, exposed value null, never fabricated). The phase text should then be made internally consistent.
findings.resolution: Took the recommendation's second branch (preserve compatibility), because it is the only option consistent with the frozen constraints: §2 'Must Not Change' (compatibility semantics), §10's failure table ('Missing score becomes 0 -> Emit null; never fabricate'), §8 T100640-03, AC-100640-02 ('omitted score is null'), and DoD 'Existing behavior remains intact'. The alternative (keep fail-closed) would have turned a display-metadata gap into an ordering change, which is exactly the compat break the finding names. Verified against the pre-change code first: `git show HEAD:crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank.rs` shows the old parser consumed only `index` for bare-array/results[] bodies (any score ignored) and errored only on non-numeric `scores[]` elements. Code: rerank_parse.rs `entry_score` now returns `Option<f64>` (first numeric under the keys, else None) and both shapes use `.map(normalize_rerank_score)`; index validation (missing/non-integer, duplicate, out-of-range) and `scores[]` numeric-element validation are unchanged (still fail-closed). Tests: rerank_tests.rs:92 `parse_keeps_entries_without_a_numeric_score_in_order` pins `[{"index":1}]` -> order [1,0,2] with all-None scores and `{"results":[{"index":2},{"index":0}]}` -> order [2,0,1] (the restored pre-change expectation); rerank_score_tests.rs:52 `parse_results_accepts_score_alias_and_keeps_unscored_entries` covers index-only, string, and null score values; rerank_score_tests.rs:138 `http_adapter_results_shape_carries_no_score_when_the_provider_omits_it` exercises the same body through the real HttpReranker over a fake server. Phase text made consistent: §5 Task 2's 'fails closed' sentence replaced with the real rule (index kept, order kept, `score: None`, exposed `null`), Completion Evidence records the decision, and Known Limitations states that a present-but-non-numeric score is treated as `null`, not a parse failure. Real output: `cargo test -p clio-retrieve --locked` -> 'test result: ok. 171 passed; 0 failed', rerank filter -> 46 passed; full `make check` exit 0; `make coverage` exit 0 with rerank_parse.rs at 100% lines / 100% functions. Conservative checks kept: `parse_rejects_malformed_bodies` still fails closed on empty body, out-of-range index, duplicate index, missing index, and non-numeric `scores[]` elements. Remediation round 2 closed the residual this fix left behind: the module-header `## Owns` bullet in `crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_parse.rs` still claimed fail-closed score validation, so it now reads "scores kept when present (`None` otherwise); fail-closed index validation and `scores[]` element validation" (header at crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_parse.rs:10-16), matching the file's own score-contract and `# Errors` sections. Green in the round-2 full runs.
findings.recommendation_adjusted: Second branch selected and implemented; recommendation now reads: preserve compatibility by carrying score: None for a present entry without a numeric score (order preserved, exposed value null, never fabricated), and keep the phase text internally consistent (done in §5, §9, §12, and the roadmap index).
findings.evidence_after: crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_parse.rs:112-175 (parser; `entry_score` at :192-195); rerank_tests.rs:92-107; rerank_score_tests.rs:52-67,138-149; phase §5/§9/§12 and roadmap index updated; module header corrected in round 2.

findings.title: No hit-level test for a provider-omitted document leaving scores.reranker null while the reranker ran (T100640-03 only covered at parser level)
findings.evidence: parse_bare_array_omitted_document_appends_in_original_order (crates/clio-retrieve/src/rerank_score_tests.rs:87) asserts score None at the parser; tei_adapter_posts_query_texts_and_pinned_raw_scores (rerank_tests.rs:135) asserts [Some, Some, None] at the adapter. The live-reranker retriever tests score every document (hybrid_rerank_tests.rs:35, stage_score_tests.rs:262) or fail outright (hybrid_rerank_tests.rs:66); the MCP fake sidecar returns a complete 2-of-2 response (crates/clio-mcp/src/index_drain_tests.rs:186-189). No test asserts a hit's scores.reranker stays null when a configured provider omits that document.
findings.recommendation: Add a retriever-level test with a live adapter response that omits one document, asserting fused order for the appended document and scores.reranker == null for it.
findings.resolution: Added exactly that test: `t08_omitted_document_appends_in_fused_order_with_null_reranker` at crates/clio-retrieve/src/hybrid_rerank_tests.rs:76. It seeds three lexical documents, captures the fused order with a plain retriever, attaches a live `HttpReranker` pointing at a one-shot fake server whose 200 body scores only shortlist indices 1 and 0 ({{"index":1,"score":0.8},{"index":0,"score":0.3}}), and asserts `out.reranked`, `ids(out) == [fused[1], fused[0], fused[2]]`, `hits[0].scores.reranker == Some(0.8)`, `hits[1].scores.reranker == Some(0.3)`, and `hits[2].scores.reranker == None` (the appended document keeps its fused place with a null value, never a fabricated one). The file's `## Owns` header was extended to cover the omitted-document case. Real output: `cargo test -p clio-retrieve --locked rerank` -> 46 passed / 0 failed including 'test hybrid_rerank_tests::t08_omitted_document_appends_in_fused_order_with_null_reranker ... ok'; full `make check` exit 0; `make coverage` exit 0 with hybrid_rerank_tests.rs path-excluded as a *_tests.rs module.
